ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or write stories. But, even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators of these neural networks and AIs, they're like the Lego builders, but they don't know the secret code, hitori no koto wa nan desu ka? (what is this one thing?)

These networks are made up of many layers, like a big onion, and each layer is connected to the next, kare wa kare ni tsuite iru (they are together). But, the way they learn and make decisions, that's like a magic trick, houdou no koto wa nan desu ka? (what is this magic?)

The creators can give the robot instructions, like "write a story about a cat," but they don't know how the robot will actually do it, nani ga shite iru ka? (what will it do?). It's like trying to predict a weather forecast, kaze no koto wa nan desu ka? (what is the weather like?)

So, even the creators of these powerful AIs, they're not entirely sure how they work, nan desu ka? (what is this?). It's like they're still learning, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind).
